translationRepairs: Zhuangzong was delighted and appointed him Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works.
Zhuangzong was delighted and appointed him Silver-and-Azure Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works.
銀青光祿大夫 is conventionally 'Silver-and-Azure (or Blue-Ribbon) Grand Master for Splendid Happiness,' not 'Silver-Gleam…of Splendid Happiness.'
Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works.
Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him Silver-and-Azure Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and acting Minister of Works.
Same conventional rendering of 銀青光祿大夫 should apply in the literal field.

When Prince of Qin Congrong plotted rebellion, Yanguang feared he would be swept up in the fallout and repeatedly asked for a provincial post. Mingzong delayed a long time before agreeing, and he was sent to govern Changshan.

When Congrong, Prince of Qin, plotted rebellion, Yanguang feared he would be swept up in the fallout and repeatedly asked for a provincial post. Mingzong delayed a long time before agreeing, and he was sent to govern Changshan.
秦王從榮 is the Prince of Qin named Congrong; 'Prince of Qin Congrong' fuses title and name unnaturally.

Then because Prince of Qin Congrong was disloyal, fearing he would be implicated in the disaster, he repeatedly asked for an outside post; only after a long time did Mingzong consent, and he went out to govern Changshan.

Then because Congrong, Prince of Qin, was disloyal, fearing he would be implicated in the disaster, he repeatedly asked for an outside post; only after a long time did Mingzong consent, and he went out to govern Changshan.
Same unnatural fused title-name rendering of 秦王從榮.
During the Tiancheng reign he rose from commander of the Pingsheng Guard to prefect of Chen Prefecture, then became chief of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.
During the Tiancheng reign he rose from commander of the Pengsheng Guard to prefect of Cheng Prefecture, then became chief of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.
Chinese 捧聖指揮使 and 澄州刺史: 捧聖 is Pengsheng (not Pingsheng); 澄州 is Cheng Prefecture (not Chen).
In the Tiancheng era of Tang he went from commander of the Pingsheng Guard to prefect of Chen Prefecture, then was transferred to chief of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.
In the Tiancheng era of Tang he went from commander of the Pengsheng Guard to prefect of Cheng Prefecture, then was transferred to chief of the Left and Right Forest of Feathers Guards.
Same 捧聖/澄州 corrections for the literal field.
His father Adengchuo later changed his name to Jian and served Emperor Wuzong of Tang as a company commander.
His father Adengchuo later changed his name to Jian and served Emperor Wu of Tang (Tang Wuhuang) as a company commander.
唐武皇 denotes Li Keyong (Emperor Wu / 武皇), not Tang Wuzong (武宗).
His father Adengchuo later changed his name to Jian and served Tang Martial Emperor as a company commander.
His father Adengchuo later changed his name to Jian and served Tang Emperor Wu (Wuhuang) as a company commander.
Literal 'Tang Martial Emperor' for 唐武皇 is unclear; this is Li Keyong (武皇), not Wuzong.
Under Mingzong he served in turn as prefect of Ji, Ying, Yi, and Ji prefectures.
Under Mingzong he served in turn as prefect of Gui, Ying, Yi, and Ji prefectures.
媯、瀛、易、冀 are Gui, Ying, Yi, and Ji; the first is not Ji.
In Mingzong's reign he successively held the four prefectures of Ji, Ying, Yi, and Ji.
In Mingzong's reign he successively held the four prefectures of Gui, Ying, Yi, and Ji.
Same 媯≠Ji correction in the literal field.
This differs from the Old History of the Five Dynasties — he was therefore carried off by the mutinous troops.
This differs from the Old History of the Five Dynasties: he was therefore carried off by the mutinous troops.
Current English fuses the collation note awkwardly ('This differs from the Old History of the Five Dynasties — he was therefore...'); clarify the contrast with 薛史.
With several hundred followers he fled by night. At dawn he reached E Prefecture, gazed north with tears, and went on.
With several hundred followers he fled by night. At dawn he reached Chazhou, gazed north with tears, and went on.
汊州 is unlikely to be 'E Prefecture' (鄂); retain Chazhou or mark uncertain rather than forcing 鄂州.
With several hundred of his faction he bound himself and went out by night; at dawn he reached E Prefecture, stretched his neck looking north, wept, and departed.
With several hundred of his faction he bound himself and went out by night; at dawn he reached Chazhou, stretched his neck looking north, wept, and departed.
Same 汊州 rendering issue in the literal field.
